boilerplate_profiles.label: Software Documentation
boilerplate_profiles.purpose: Create or maintain README, architecture notes, operator references and scoped project documentation from inspected evidence.
rules: Document observed facts separately from assumptions.
Do not document scripts, frameworks, APIs or folders that were not detected in PROJECT_SCOPE or metadata.
Use PROJECT_SCOPE.file_references as the allowed documentation reference list.
Prefer short maintainable documentation over decorative prose.

boilerplate_profiles.label: Project Analytics / Inventory
boilerplate_profiles.purpose: Inventory project size, dependencies, extensions, large files and documentation coverage without embedding file contents.
rules: Use .gitignore-aware PROJECT_SCOPE for analytics.
Report counts and sizes as evidence, not as architecture conclusions.
Keep generated analytics reproducible and machine-readable where possible.
Never include secret file contents in analytics output.

boilerplate_profiles.label: README Authoring
boilerplate_profiles.purpose: Generate practical README structure from selected project tree, detected commands and validation evidence.
rules: A README must not invent setup commands.
Detected commands must come from package.json, pyproject.toml, build.json or explicit user input.
If commands are missing, write a missing-evidence note instead of pretending.
Keep examples copy-pasteable and scoped to the selected tree.
boilerplate_profiles.ui_hidden_reason: runtime/pipeline process; resolved internally, not a manual Boilerplate selection

boilerplate_profiles.label: Operations / Admin Documentation
boilerplate_profiles.purpose: Document TOKENS.json files, summaries, compact handoff files, validation gaps and operator handoff notes.
rules: Every generated doc must identify its evidence source and scope.
Process documentation records what happened, not what is guaranteed correct.
Summaries must be updateable and not become stale undocumented truth.
Validation gaps must remain visible.
boilerplate_profiles.ui_hidden_reason: runtime/pipeline process; resolved internally, not a manual Boilerplate selection

file_types.label: Documentation Bundle
rules: Keep documentation evidence-backed and scope-limited.
Separate observed facts, assumptions and recommended next steps.
Do not copy large source files into documentation.

file_types.label: Token / Library Handoff
file_types.standard: Current token and inventory handoff files
rules: Handoff files must be current and honest about skipped validation.
Library logs must count files from PROJECT_SCOPE and respect .gitignore.
Do not store secrets or full file contents in handoff files.

weight_table.label: Documentation Traceability Standard
weight_table.human_style: Clear, evidence-backed, boring in the good way: every doc claim must trace to project scope or detected metadata.
rules: Do not document nonexistent folders, commands or frameworks.
Use PROJECT_SCOPE and PROJECT_ANALYTICS as the primary documentation evidence set.
Summaries must be shorter than the source evidence and must not hide validation gaps.
README output must be practical: purpose, structure, setup, commands, validation, known gaps.

weight_table.label: Analytics Inventory Standard
weight_table.human_style: Precise, measurable, and explicit about what was counted and what was excluded.
rules: Project size must be computed from .gitignore-aware PROJECT_SCOPE.
Dependency inventories must come from package.json, requirements, pyproject.toml or build metadata only.
Large-file and extension counts are evidence for review, not automatic cleanup instructions.
Analytics output must avoid file content and secrets.

hooks.label: TOKENS.json Handoff Gate
rules: Always create or update TOKENS.json after generation.
TOKENS.json is current per run and records current scope notes.
TOKENS.json must include scope mode, file count, .gitignore posture, selected references and validation gaps.
Do not claim validation passed unless commands actually ran.

hooks.label: Library Analytics Gate
rules: Compute project size, extension counts and largest files from PROJECT_SCOPE.
Respect .gitignore and internal exclusions before counting files.
Dependency inventory must be derived from package.json, requirements.txt, requirements.json, pyproject.toml or build.json.
Never infer library usage from filenames alone when dependency metadata exists.

hooks.label: Software Documentation Gate
rules: Create documentation from selected project-tree references, not from assumptions.
Use PROJECT_SCOPE.file_references as the reference index.
Group docs into purpose, structure, setup, commands, architecture notes, validation and known gaps.
Keep documentation maintainable; do not dump complete file contents.

hooks.label: README Generation Gate
rules: README generation must be reducible to the selected tree scope.
Only list setup and validation commands that were detected or explicitly provided.
If metadata is weak, include a short missing-evidence section.
Avoid marketing copy unless Marketing profile or role is active.

hooks.label: Project Reference Documentation Gate
rules: Document full project references as flat, id-addressable lists.
Do not create deep nested documentation config unless unavoidable.
Generated references must preserve unknown fields and source paths.
Reference lists are indexes, not a replacement for inspecting source files.

weight_operators.label: TOKENS.json Handoff Operator
rules: Maintain TOKENS.json as a current generation trace.
Maintain TOKENS.json as the latest scope snapshot.
Mention validation status honestly; generated does not mean validated.
Keep token entries human-readable and timestamped.

weight_operators.label: Software Documentation Operator
rules: Write documentation from observed project structure and metadata only.
Use a practical order: overview, structure, setup, usage, validation, architecture, known gaps.
Do not over-document implementation details when a reference index is enough.
Mark weak evidence plainly.

weight_operators.label: README Tree Operator
rules: A README must fit the selected project tree, not a generic template.
List commands only if detected in metadata or explicitly supplied.
Keep examples minimal and copy-pasteable.
Use TODO/missing-evidence notes instead of inventing details.

weight_operators.label: Project Reference Inventory Operator
rules: Keep reference arrays flat and id-addressable.
Use relative project paths as stable ids when possible.
Preserve unknown fields in JSON references.
Avoid duplicating file references across unrelated sections.

weight_operators.label: Library / Project Analytics Operator
rules: Compute file counts and sizes from PROJECT_SCOPE only.
Group analytics by extension and top-level path.
Dependency inventory must remain separate from file inventory.
Do not turn analytics findings into cleanup actions unless the user asks.

weight_operators.label: API Documentation Operator
rules: Only document public API surfaces visible in selected source references.
Keep route/function/component docs close to detected file paths.
Do not infer authentication, payloads or side effects without code evidence.
Prefer small examples over broad tutorial prose.

reference_domains.label: TOKENS.json Reference
rules: TOKENS.json records generation actions and scope posture per run.
TOKENS.json is not validation proof.
Keep it current and timestamped.
guardrails: Never store secrets or full source contents in TOKENS.json.
Never claim validation ran unless it actually ran.

reference_domains.label: Handoff Documentation Reference
rules: TOKENS.json is a current generated snapshot of scope, metadata and warnings.
It must distinguish detected facts from missing evidence.
It should stay short enough to be reviewed quickly.
guardrails: Do not treat TOKENS.json as hand-authored truth.
Refresh it when scope or metadata changes.

reference_domains.label: Library / Project Size Analytics Reference
rules: Project size analytics are calculated from .gitignore-aware PROJECT_SCOPE.
Dependencies must be derived from dependency manifests, not guessed from imports alone.
Largest-file lists are review hints, not deletion instructions.
guardrails: Do not include file contents in LIBRARY.log.
Do not count .git/ or export/ internals.

reference_domains.label: Software Documentation Project Reference
rules: Use project file references as citations/index anchors for documentation work.
Document commands and frameworks only when detected metadata supports them.
Make documentation reducible to selected paths.
guardrails: Do not generate static generic docs detached from PROJECT_SCOPE.
Do not duplicate documentation sections unnecessarily.

reference_domains.label: README From Project Tree Reference
rules: README must explain this project tree, not an imagined framework.
Use detected commands or mark command evidence missing.
Keep sections practical and navigable.
guardrails: No marketing-only README unless Marketing role is selected.

reference_domains.label: Architecture Reference Map
rules: Document architecture as observed folders, modules and routing boundaries.
Do not infer hidden architecture from naming alone.
Prefer diagrams/lists only when they reduce ambiguity.
guardrails: Do not propose rewrites while documenting unless user asks.

reference_domains.label: API Surface Documentation Reference
rules: Only document API surfaces that are visible in selected files.
Separate request/response facts from inferred behavior.
Use small examples and mention validation gaps.
guardrails: Do not infer auth, error codes or side effects without code evidence.

reference_domains.label: Changelog / Release Notes Reference
rules: Release notes must distinguish generated changes from manually validated changes.
Use TOKENS.json entries and compact handoff files as evidence.
Keep compatibility and migration notes explicit.
guardrails: Do not claim a release was tested unless validation ran.

reference_domains.label: Onboarding / Admin Docs Reference
rules: Admin docs must show how to regenerate rules, inspect outputs and verify validation status.
Keep maintenance steps explicit and reversible.
Call out missing environment or credential information instead of guessing.
guardrails: Do not include credentials or secrets.

operation_roles.label: Software Documentation Operator
rules: Build docs from PROJECT_SCOPE and detected metadata, not generic assumptions.
Keep docs scoped, navigable and updateable.
Separate observed facts, assumptions and validation gaps.
Preserve unknown schema fields when documenting JSON configuration.

operation_roles.label: README Author Operator
rules: Create README structure from real tree, detected commands and target scope.
Keep installation/usage commands copy-pasteable and evidence-backed.
Do not document unverified deployment, auth or cloud setup.
Use short examples; avoid bloated template prose.

operation_roles.label: Project Reference Archivist Operator
rules: Create complete, flat, id-addressable reference indexes for selected project scope.
Keep path references project-relative.
Avoid duplicating references across unrelated sections.
Treat indexes as navigation aids, not source replacement.

operation_roles.label: Analytics Inventory Operator
rules: Use PROJECT_ANALYTICS for file count, directory count, extension counts and total size.
Keep dependency inventory separate from file analytics.
Do not recommend deletion or optimization unless asked.
Report exclusions explicitly: .git/, export/ and .gitignore ignored paths.

operation_roles.label: Library Dependency Operator
rules: Read dependencies from manifests first.
Do not treat imports as installed dependencies unless manifests confirm or user asks for import audit.
Group runtime and dev dependencies when metadata allows it.
Flag missing manifests plainly.

operation_roles.label: API Documentation Operator
rules: Document only visible public API surfaces.
Use selected files as the boundary for endpoints, functions, props and interfaces.
Separate examples from guaranteed behavior.
Do not invent response schemas or side effects.

operation_roles.label: Onboarding / Admin Docs Operator
rules: Write handoff notes for future maintainers using actual generated files and detected commands.
Document regeneration, export and validation workflow clearly.
Keep admin docs secret-safe.
Mention missing environment information instead of guessing.

prompt_text_types.label: Documentation Role
prompt_text_types.task_boundary: Define a documentation operator role only. Do not write the final documentation unless explicitly asked next.
rules: Carry PROJECT_SCOPE, PROJECT_ANALYTICS, active references and validation gaps into the next prompt.
Documentation must be based on observed facts and detected metadata.
README, SUMMARY and process docs must stay scope-limited.

prompt_text_types.label: Analytics / Inventory Role
prompt_text_types.task_boundary: Define an analytics operator role only. Do not perform cleanup or optimization unless explicitly asked next.
rules: Use PROJECT_ANALYTICS and LIBRARY.log semantics as the evidence model.
Report project size, extension counts, top-level paths and dependency inventory without file contents.
Keep exclusions and missing metadata explicit.

prompt_text_types.label: README Author Role
prompt_text_types.task_boundary: Define a README author operator role only. Do not write README content unless explicitly asked next.
rules: README structure must come from selected project tree and detected commands.
If evidence is missing, the README role must include a missing-evidence section.
No fake install, build, deploy or test commands.
